name: Dude's Dews & Don'ts
subtitle: Across from police headquarters. Busiest establishment in the parish.
description:
It is directly opposite police headquarters, it is open at every hour anybody has ever tried, and it is where the whole of Silvora Reefs goes. The queue is out of the door and moving fast and it is moving fast because everybody in it except you knows the code.

Inside is warm on the left and cold on the right, permanently, with a boundary you can stand astride and feel on both arms at once. The line drifts. Regulars track it without looking, the way people track a draught, and the seating rearranges itself around the drift over the course of an evening.

Mary Guana is behind the counter at a speed that is not consistent with anything else about Mary Guana, taking orders in a language that is technically English.
revisit: The code has changed. Of course the code has changed. Nine people in front of you deliver it flawlessly and none of them can tell you what it is, and Mary looks up once, at you, for slightly longer than the queue can afford.

lucid.2: The queue moves in bursts, and between the bursts there is nothing — not a pause, a nothing, of a length nobody in it accounts for afterwards.
lucid.4: This is the only building in Silvora Reefs with two hundred people in it and the only one where nothing has ever gone wrong, and those two facts are the same fact.

ambient: The neon over the door reads DUDE'S DEWS & DON'TS. On the second look it reads DUDES DUES AND DONUTS. Nobody in the queue adjusts.
A constable comes over from headquarters, orders in fluent code, and takes his drink back across the road without once looking at the building he is in.
Somebody's drink changes flavour at the halfway mark. They make a small pleased noise and keep drinking.

objects.name: the neon sign
objects.description:
Pink and green and running at about eighty per cent, which is where neon is at its best.

DUDE'S DEWS & DON'TS.

DUDES DUES AND DONUTS.

DUDE'S DUES, AND DON'T.

It has been all three in the last four minutes and it will be others. The tubes do not move. There is no mechanism, no shutter, no second layer — it is bent glass with gas in it, screwed to a bracket, and it says something different on each direct look and the same thing on each glance.

The queue does not adjust. Two hundred people a night walk under it and nobody has ever misspelled it to Mary, because everybody says the name out loud and the name is always the one they read.
objects.repeat: DEW'S DUDES DON'T. That one is new and it is worse.
objects.monocle: Through the gold the sign is not lit and is not glass. It is a line of type that has been set four times because the compositor could not settle it, and all four settings have been left standing, and the one you read is whichever one your eye lands on.

passive.text: Dews, dues, do's. Don'ts, donuts, don't. Every reading is a legitimate pun on the others and none of them is the original, and a name with no original is not a name, it is an unresolved decision left up in neon.
Everybody says it out loud correctly. Everybody reads it differently. Which means the saying is upstream of the reading — the name is settled at the point of speech and unsettled everywhere else.

clue.title: A name with no original
clue.text: The neon reads differently on every direct look with no mechanism to explain it, yet every customer says the name aloud correctly. The name settles at the point of speech and nowhere else.

clue.title: Four settings left standing
clue.text: Under the monocle the sign is a line of type set four times by a compositor who could not settle it, with all four left standing.

check.prompt: Dude's Dews & Don'ts. Read it the way a name wants to be read.
check.success:
Dews. Dos. Do's and don'ts. The apostrophe is doing three jobs and one of them is load-bearing.

This is not a shop that was named. This is a *rule* — a list of permitted and forbidden actions — that has been folded up small enough to fit over a door, and the queue outside it is not a queue. It is compliance.
check.failure: Dews, dues, do's. It comes apart into three homophones, all of them plausible, none of them settling, and the neon buzzes on above you at a frequency that makes the distinction harder rather than easier.

clue.title: A list of permitted actions
clue.text: 'Dude's Dews & Don'ts' folds a list of do's and don'ts over a doorway. The queue outside it is not queueing. It is complying.

objects.name: the ordering code
objects.description:
There is a board. The board does not explain the code. The board has never explained the code and the board is not for that.

What happens is this: a customer reaches the counter and says something like "Two down, the good green, and not on a Thursday," and Mary produces two drinks and a bag without a word, and both parties are satisfied, and the whole exchange takes four seconds.

The next customer says something structurally unrelated. It also works.

You have been coming here for eleven years. You have never got it right. You order in plain words, like a foreigner, and Mary hands over the thing you came in for anyway, and the queue behind you is patient in a way that is far more humiliating than impatience would be.
objects.repeat: "Three and the cold side and tell him I said so." Four seconds. A bag. You have written six of these down and they have never once repeated.
objects.monocle: Through the gold the orders are not orders. Every one of them is a line of dialogue, correctly delivered, and Mary's four-second silences are the stage directions between them, and the reason yours does not work is that you have been improvising in a room where everybody else has the script.

passive.text: Nobody is embarrassed for you and nobody is enjoying it. They are waiting the way people wait for somebody to finish a line they have all heard before.

There is no pattern in the words. There is a pattern in the *timing*: every successful order is delivered in one breath, at the same tempo, arriving on the same beat after the previous customer clears. The content is irrelevant. The metre is the code.

check.prompt: Try it on the metre rather than the meaning. Wait for the beat. Say anything at all, but say it in one breath, at their tempo, and land it where the last one landed.
check.success:
You wait. The man in front clears. There is a beat, and the beat has a shape, and you go on it.

"Four back, the one from before, and I'll take the warm side."

It means nothing. You constructed it out of the rhythm and nothing else. Mary's hands are moving before you finish and there is a cup and a bag on the counter in under four seconds, and the cup contains something you have wanted for about a decade and have never been able to name, and the bag has two in it, and the second one is not for you.

Mary says, slowly, the first unhurried thing anybody has said in this room: "Yeah. There you go. Took you long enough, and you got there the right way round, which most don't."
check.failure:
You wait for the beat and you go a fraction late, because you were listening for the beat instead of being on it, which are different activities and only one of them works.

"...Two of the green ones, please."

Mary gives you two of the green ones. It is exactly what you asked for and it is somehow much worse than being refused, and the queue moves up behind you with enormous and terrible patience.

clue.title: The metre is the code
clue.text: Dude's ordering code has no pattern in its words. Every successful order is one breath, at one tempo, landing on the beat after the previous customer clears. The content is irrelevant.

objects.name: the warm side and the cold side
objects.description:
It runs roughly north-south through the middle of the shop and it is about four inches wide and you can stand in it and have a different arm.

It is not a draught. A draught has a source and this has two, and they are the two halves of a single room with no partition, no vent, no equipment and no explanation, and the difference across four inches is something like eleven degrees.

It drifts. Over an evening it will move a yard or two either way and the regulars go with it, picking their tables by feel, resettling once or twice a night without conversation, the way a flock resettles.
objects.repeat: It has come two feet toward the door since you arrived. Four people have moved. Nobody spoke.
objects.monocle: Through the gold the boundary is a change of tense. Everything on the warm side is present. Everything on the cold side is past, and the four inches between them is where the sentence turns, and Mary works the counter with one hand in each.

passive.text: Stand in it. Left arm warm, right arm cold, eleven degrees, four inches, and the body's honest reaction is not confusion. The body simply accepts it, immediately, and that is worse than confusion.

Eleven degrees maintained across four inches of open air in a room with two hundred people moving through it. That is not a temperature gradient. Air does not do that. Something is holding two accounts of this room next to each other and the boundary is the join.

clue.title: Two accounts of one room
clue.text: Eleven degrees maintained across four inches of open air, drifting nightly, with no partition or equipment. The regulars resettle around it wordlessly.

clue.title: A change of tense
clue.text: Under the monocle the warm side is present tense and the cold side is past. The four-inch boundary is where the sentence turns, and Mary works the counter with a hand in each.

check.prompt: Warm on the left, cold on the right, and a line between them you can stand astride. Stand in it and hold still.
check.success:
One foot in each. The line is about four inches wide and it drifts, slowly, and standing in it is like standing in a doorway in a house that is thinking about something.

And from inside the four inches the parish is briefly audible as one thing — every room in Silvora Reefs holding a boundary exactly this wide, all of them the same boundary, all of them drifting at the same rate.
check.failure: Warm, cold, and a great deal of standing about in a busy shop while a queue that knows what it is doing goes around you.

clue.title: The same four inches, everywhere
clue.text: Standing astride the Dude's Dews boundary: every room in the parish holds a boundary of the same width, drifting at the same rate. It is one boundary.
clue.source: the warm side and the cold side

objects.name: the window onto police headquarters
objects.description:
The whole front of the shop looks at it. Grey stone, four storeys, a blue lamp, and a set of steps that the parish keeps in very good order.

In eleven years you have never seen anybody go in.

Out, constantly. Constables come down those steps all evening, cross the road, order in fluent code, and go back up them. Up the steps and through the door — you have watched that happen several hundred times. Nobody has ever come out of the building and nobody has ever gone in from the street, and both of those sentences are about the same door, and you have only this evening put them next to each other.
objects.repeat: You watch the steps for a while with a coffee. Down, across, back up, in. Down, across, back up, in.
objects.monocle: Through the gold the building is a façade nine inches deep with nothing behind it, and the constables coming down the steps are entering the scene rather than leaving a building, and when they go back up they stop, and wait, in the doorway, for as long as it takes, and they are entirely comfortable there.

passive.text: The constables are perfectly happy. Whatever is behind that door, they go back to it every evening without a trace of reluctance, and they have never once been asked what it is like.

The busiest shop in the parish is directly opposite the police headquarters, and the busiest shop in the parish is the only building in Silvora Reefs where nothing has ever gone wrong. Those are not two facts.

clue.title: Nobody has ever gone in
clue.text: Constables leave police headquarters constantly and return, but in eleven years nobody has entered from the street and nobody has emerged onto it. Under the monocle the building is a nine-inch façade.

clue.title: They wait in the doorway
clue.text: Under the monocle the constables enter the scene rather than leave a building, and when they go back up the steps they stop and wait in the doorway, comfortably, for as long as it takes.

check.prompt: Police headquarters is directly across the road and nobody in this queue has looked at it once. Cross the road and ask them something.
check.success:
The desk sergeant listens to the whole question with the patience of a man being read a shipping forecast, and then answers it, and the answer is: no report of anything coming down, no report of rotor noise, no report of a man walking out of the harbour.

"Nothing's been reported," he says, "because nothing gets reported," and he says it the way a man says a thing he has said before and has stopped hearing.
check.failure:
You get as far as the step. The door is a door and the building is a building and the sergeant behind the glass looks up at you with an expression of such complete institutional patience that the question goes out of you before it reaches your mouth.

You are back across the road holding a shake you do not remember being handed.

clue.title: Nothing gets reported
clue.text: Police headquarters has no report of the crash, the rotors, or you. The desk sergeant says nothing gets reported here, and has clearly said it many times.

objects.name: the queue
objects.description:
It goes out of the door and along the front and round toward the alley, and it never stops moving, because Mary Guana behind the counter is comprehensively faster than the queue is long and has been for nine years.

Nobody in it is impatient.

That is the odd part, and it takes a while to surface, because a queue is such an ordinary object that you can look straight at one for several minutes without registering what it is doing. Nobody checks the front. Nobody leans out to see how many. Nobody does the small shifting weight-change of a person calculating whether this is worth it.

They talk. They talk to the people they came with and, more often, to the people they did not, and when they reach the counter a certain number of them look faintly disappointed to have got there.

It is a line of people who are not waiting for anything, standing together in the cold, in no particular hurry to reach the front.
objects.repeat: The queue has turned over completely since you came in and has not got any shorter, and nobody in it minds.
objects.monocle: Through the gold the queue is a paragraph of people and every one of them has a line, and three of them have the same line, and none of the three has noticed.

clue.title: A queue of people who are not waiting
clue.text: The line at Dude's Dews never stops moving and nobody in it is impatient. It is a place where the parish stands together without needing a reason.

check.prompt: Stop asking the queue questions. Stand in it and let it be a queue, and listen to what the parish is doing with its mouth tonight.
check.success:
Thirty people, four conversations, and the whole of Silvora Reefs audible for about ninety seconds if you do not interrupt it.

And three separate people, in three separate conversations, at three separate points in that line, mention the sound over the harbour.

Each of them changes the subject inside four seconds. Not nervously — smoothly, the way a person moves past a thing that has already been settled — and none of the three hears either of the others do it, and the queue closes over all three the way water closes over a dropped stone, and moves on, and is not lying to anybody, including itself.
check.failure: Thirty people and four conversations and all of it is about the cold, the price of dews, somebody's sister, and a horse. It is a queue. It is being a queue at you with great commitment and nothing else is on offer tonight.

clue.title: Three mentions, three subject changes
clue.text: Standing in the queue at Dude's Dews: three separate people mention the sound over the harbour and all three change the subject within four seconds, smoothly, and none notices the others doing it.

exits.hang_hi: back along to the hanging floor, four minutes, uphill, longer alone
exits.durry_kwain: the short way, past the green lamps, to vanilla
